essence.one_sentence: A lava lamp is a small heat engine in glass: a bulb warms the wax, the wax loses density and climbs, cools and falls again, so the light and the motion come from one source.
essence.summary: Glass vessel, a bulb glow from below, and slow wax that stretches, pinches off, merges and sinks in a loop.

llm_brief.text:
On the table: a lava lamp is a glass vessel over a bulb base, holding wax and a clear or translucent liquid. The bulb warms the wax, its density drops, it rises, cools and sinks back, and a wire coil in the base lets cooled blobs merge again. That cycle is the object. Blobs stretch as they lift, pinch off, pool and merge at the bottom or top, and part again. The few measured facts: the bulb is incandescent or halogen, and no source gives a period for the rise or sink.

Ways in: a classic tapered bottle on a round bulb base, warm wax in clear liquid. A rounded globe with a short neck and small cap. A silver hourglass base with bright wax in violet liquid. A tall tapered lamp with a cap and tinted violet liquid. A squat round lamp or short cylinder on a base, with a few large blobs.

Dials: a rise over 20 s reads as near-still, and one under 4 s reads as a jolt; 8 to 16 s up and 5 to 12 s down is a starting spread, tuned by eye; a warm-up of 30 to 90 s before the first rise. Frame height is 0.6 to 0.9 of the picture when the lamp is tall in frame, 0.25 to 0.4 in a wide scene. Easing runs from ease-in-out for the usual wax feel, to ease-out on the lift and ease-in on the sink, varied per blob. A linear curve reads as a sprite, and an overshoot reads as a rubber toy.

Worn paths: the usual move for the word lava is molten rock; fresher: a decorative glass light object with wax inside. The usual move for the word lamp is an oil or street lamp; fresher: a glass object with its own light. The usual move for motion is a still gradient; fresher options: a heat-driven rise and sink, where wax peels off the base and climbs; a staggered drift, where blobs leave the base at different times; or a settled base that climbs in a sheet before it breaks into blobs. The usual move for the rise is a springy bounce; fresher: a slow, heavy curve. The usual move for colour is a rainbow of wax; fresher: one saturated warm hue in a deeper liquid of its own family.

Open: the rise and sink timing, the start state (three options: a settled base with a warm-up, a mid-motion start, or an evenly dispersed start), the size and frame, the colours, and whether the lamp responds to a click.

ak-lava-molten.excluded_sense: molten rock, volcanic flow, a volcano
ak-lava-molten.instead: the wax and liquid blobs inside a decorative lamp

ak-lamp-oil.excluded_sense: an oil or kerosene lamp; a street lamp post
ak-lamp-oil.instead: a decorative glass light object with wax and liquid inside

ak-no-vessel.instead: A tapered glass vessel with visible walls, a bulb glow in its base, and solid-looking wax inside.

ak-static-gradient.instead: Wax that rises, stretches, pinches off and sinks in a slow loop.

ak-neon-rainbow-wax.instead: Wax in one saturated warm hue, in a deeper liquid of its own family, lit from below.

ak-wax-stays-low.term: wax that never leaves the base
ak-wax-stays-low.instead: wax settles at the base, then peels off and climbs in a slow sheet

ak-bouncing-ball.instead: blobs drift up, then fall quickly (3 to 5 s, a release) or sink slowly (5 to 12 s, weight)

k-lamp-reads-lamp.text: Does a stranger name it a lamp at a glance, a glass object with wax inside, rather than volcanic lava or an oil lamp?

test.spec: Show the first rendered frame to a reader who has not seen the prompt and ask what the object is.

k-vessel-walls.text: Does the wax sit inside a glass vessel with visible walls, a base and a cap, rather than a free glowing blob?

test.spec: Base, vessel walls and cap are all visible in the frame at rest.

k-glow-from-base.text: Does the glow come from the base, brightest at the bottom and fading toward the cap?

test.spec: Sample the luminance of the vessel from bottom to top; it falls toward the cap.

k-rest-state.text: How does the first frame read: wax pooled at the base, wax spread evenly through the liquid, or blobs already moving? Which of the three start states does it match, and does it read as the one intended?

test.spec: Capture the first frame before any warm-up and ask a reader which of the three start states it looks like: settled base with warm-up, mid-motion start, or evenly dispersed start.

k-rise-and-sink-loop.text: Does wax leave the base, climb, and sink back, so that the motion repeats as a loop?

test.spec: Watch 60 s of motion; at least one blob rises past the middle of the vessel and comes back down.

k-heavy-curve.text: Does the wax move in a heavy, slow curve rather than a springy hop or a straight slide?

test.spec: Track one blob's vertical position over time; its speed changes through each move and it does not overshoot the top.

k-merge-and-split.text: Do blobs stretch before they break free, and merge and part again near the top or bottom?

test.spec: Watch for a blob that narrows before it pinches off, and for a merge near an end of the vessel.

k-blob-variety.text: Do the blobs differ in size and speed, so that no two read as copies?

test.spec: Count distinct blob radii in one frame; expect at least three sizes across the blobs.

k-one-hue.text: Does the wax read in one saturated hue inside a deeper liquid of its family, rather than a rainbow of wax?

test.spec: Count the hues on the wax: one hue, and the liquid a deeper shade of its family.

k-filler-words.text: Does the page copy avoid the filler words stunning, masterpiece and seamless?

q-rise-timing.text: How long do one rise and one sink take?
q-rise-timing.resolve: a found video with frame-diff timing (no fetched source here states a timing); the spreads are in mo-timing

q-start-state.text: What state does the motion start in?
options: settled base start with warm-up: wax pooled at the base with the bulb off, then a warm-up before the first rise, which reads as a lamp coming on
mid-motion start: blobs already rising and sinking, which reads as a lamp already running
evenly dispersed start: wax spread through the liquid before the coil pulls it into blobs, which reads as a lamp just switched on
q-start-state.resolve: builder choice; no source gives a start state

u-lava-lamp.text: The whole request is the object: a lava lamp. Nothing else is named, so the form, colours, size and interactivity are open.

object_principles._about: Discipline primer for a lit object: how it separates from its room, how slow motion reads as calm, how a fluid rises and sinks, and how a drawn lamp goes wrong. Options and principles, not rules; the consumer decides how far to take each.

op-light-falloff.text: One dominant source with a steep falloff makes the lit object the focus; even fill flattens it.
behaviors: Light from a bulb at the base brightens the bottom of the vessel most and fades toward the cap
A falloff curve that drops quickly away from the bulb keeps the room dim and the lamp dominant
Two equal lights on the lamp give a flat, product-catalogue look rather than a glowing object
op-light-falloff.principle: Lighting that tells you where the source is makes the object feel lit rather than painted.
signals: brightest point at the bottom of the vessel

kin-slow-in-out.text: Motion that starts and stops gradually reads as natural; the frames bunch at the start and end of a move.
behaviors: A wax blob that eases out of its rest position moves slowly first and speeds up through the middle
A blob that eases into the top slows before it stops, so the rise does not look like a hit
Easing applied to every blob at the same curve makes the whole lamp feel mechanical
kin-slow-in-out.principle: Real masses take time to speed up and slow down; the eye expects that and reads its absence as wrong.
signals: every blob on the same curve

op-figure-ground.text: A lit object separates from its room by value contrast and edge light more than by outline.
behaviors: A bright wax blob reads as a light source only when the surrounding glass and room are darker
A soft halo on the wall pushes the lamp forward; a hard-edged shape pins it flat
Glow spilling onto the room separates the object from it where the vessel alone would blend in
op-figure-ground.principle: The eye reads the brightest, most contrasted region first, so the object does best when it owns that region.
signals: uniform brightness across vessel and wall

phys-simple-principles.text: The physics is a few simple principles; getting a real lamp to behave is the hard part, which is why hand-made imitations are rarely convincing.
phys-simple-principles.principle: Simple physics, finicky tuning: plausible motion comes from getting the balance right.
signals: motion that looks random but stays cohesive

op-failure-modes.term: how a drawn lamp looks fake
op-failure-modes.rung: object and lighting design, kinetic objects, fluid behaviour
op-failure-modes.text: A drawn lamp looks fake first in its motion and its glow, before its shape: the eye checks timing and falloff first.
behaviors: Blobs that slide in straight lines at one speed look like sprites, not wax
Identical blob sizes and shapes repeat visibly, so the lamp reads as a pattern
A glow that is a flat gradient with no bulb source reads as a drawn overlay on the vessel
Blobs that rise without changing shape or merging look like balloons on strings
op-failure-modes.principle: Viewers judge a lamp by how its wax moves and glows; the static form is judged second.
signals: glow not tied to the base

kin-ease-play.text: Slow motion reads as calm through its pacing. Two options: a repeating heat cycle reads as a loop, and a staggered cycle with no two blobs in step reads as a living fluid.
behaviors: A repeating heat cycle with matched timings reads as a loop, a steady and predictable rhythm
A staggered cycle with no two blobs in step reads as a living fluid, with timing that varies from blob to blob
A blob that pauses for a beat at the top before sinking reads as weight
A slow rise over many seconds with a quicker sink reads as a convecting fluid rather than a slideshow
kin-ease-play.principle: Pacing sets the reading: a repeating cycle reads as a loop, a staggered cycle reads as a living fluid.
signals: matched timings reading as a repeated loop
a pause at the top before the sink

anatomy_facts._about: Collected facts about the classic lamp: parts and materials, the heat and rise cycle, why the two fluids stay apart, the balance of heat and size, and the history. From the Wikipedia article, a university thermofluids page, Gizmodo's explainer and the Mathmos heritage pages. Each quote is copied from the cached chunk.

an-bulb.text: A classic lamp puts a standard incandescent or halogen bulb under a tall, often tapered, glass bottle.
behaviors: Heating the bottle is what lets the wax change density
an-bulb.principle: The light and the heat are the same source, so the glow and the motion come together.

af-history.text: Invented in 1963 by Edward Craven Walker, first sold as the Astro, made in Poole, Dorset since then, and renamed as Mathmos in 1992.
behaviors: The precursor was an egg timer built from a cocktail shaker, so the classic lamp grew from a two-liquid bubbling toy
The American licence became Lava Lite, a separate maker line from the British one
af-history.principle: The classic object is a British 1960s product with a long unbroken manufacturing line, and most drawn versions borrow its look from that era.

af-cycle.text: Wax is lighter than its liquid when warm, so it rises when the bulb warms it, and it sinks again as it cools, in a convection loop driven by density.
behaviors: Once the wax is less dense than the water it rises, so the rise starts only after the wax is warm enough
Heavy agitation while the wax is melted makes the mix cloudy, and it clears only after many heat cycles
af-cycle.principle: Rise and sink are the same process run in both directions: heat lowers density, cooling restores it, and the wax returns to the base.
signals: blobs that stretch and pinch off
merge at the top or bottom

tokens.density_threshold: specific gravity below 1 makes wax float up

an-parts.term: parts of a classic lava lamp
an-parts.text: A glass vessel holding wax and a clear or translucent liquid, set on a base that carries the bulb.
behaviors: The base's bulb supplies the heat that starts the cycle
Wax and liquid sit inside the vessel and respond to that heat
The coil breaks the surface tension of cooled blobs so they can merge again
an-parts.principle: The base supplies the heat; the wax and liquid carry the motion.
signals: wax settled at the bottom when cool

an-materials.text: A 1968 US patent formula mixed water with mineral oil, paraffin wax and carbon tetrachloride. Plain wax floats in water at any temperature, so the carbon tetrachloride is what lets the wax sink when cool.
behaviors: Common wax floats in water at any temperature
Carbon tetrachloride raises the wax's density at room temperature so it can sink when cool
an-materials.principle: The wax is tuned to sit a little lighter than the liquid, so small heat changes flip it.

an-motion-cycle.text: Heat lowers the wax's density and it rises; as it cools it sinks; a wire coil in the base breaks the surface tension so blobs merge and the cycle repeats.
behaviors: Warm wax floats up through the liquid; cooled wax loses buoyancy and falls back to the bottom
Wax specific gravity sits close to the liquid's, so small heat changes decide whether a blob rises or drops
Without the coil, the wax would gather into one glob that rises and falls like an elevator
an-motion-cycle.principle: Buoyancy flips with temperature: warm wax rises, cooled wax sinks.
signals: blobs pooling and merging at the bottom

an-variants-and-trade.text: US-market lamps dropped carbon tetrachloride in 1970, the current US formula is a trade secret, and a 2015 design swaps the wax for ferrofluid.
properties: no carbon tetrachloride since 1970 for the US
behaviors: Ferrofluid replaces wax in the 2015 design, so the blob look can come from a different medium
an-variants-and-trade.principle: The look survives a change of medium, so the motion is what carries the object.
signals: metallic or dark blobs in a ferrofluid lamp
clear fluid with no solvent smell in later US lamps

phys-mixing.text: The lamp's two fluids are kept from mixing by mismatched polarity: water is polar, oil is non-polar, so they separate.
behaviors: Oil and water separate cleanly under all sorts of conditions
phys-mixing.principle: Opposite polarity keeps the fluids from blending into one blob.

phys-engineering-balance.text: The lamp must balance coil heat, the temperature gradient through the water and the vessel's dimensions so the wax can cool before it sinks.
behaviors: Wax needs enough distance above the coil to cool before it returns to the bottom
phys-engineering-balance.principle: Heat, gradient and size are tuned together; no one of them sets the motion alone.
signals: wax cooling in the upper third of the vessel

exemplars._about: Makers and drawn versions with what transfers. Mix famous and deep cut. Brand names live in the term and sources only.

ex-astro.term: Astro, the classic British glass lamp
ex-astro.text: The reference object: a tapered glass vessel, wax and liquid, a bulb base, in continuous production since 1963.
behaviors: Transfers the proportion of a slim vessel and the slow rise
Does not transfer any brand motif or label
ex-astro.principle: A drawn lamp reads as this object when the vessel tapers and the wax is opaque against a clear fluid.

ex-lava-lite-us.text: The American version, sold under its own name after the US rights were bought in 1965, and later made in China and sold under other brands.
behaviors: Shows that the object was made by several makers under different names, so a generic lamp need not match one brand
ex-lava-lite-us.principle: Several makers share one object type, so the shape alone does not identify a single maker.

ex-column-marcelis.term: Column, a three-metre giant by a designer for Mathmos
ex-column-marcelis.text: A giant version with a matte aluminium body and a frosted glass vessel, so the wax glows softly rather than reading as sharp blobs.
properties: pale pink, peach and green wax
behaviors: Diffused glass turns hard blob edges into soft light
Pale wax colours read as glow at scale
Pale wax gives a milky, soft glow rather than a saturated one
ex-column-marcelis.principle: Frosting the vessel changes the lamp from a sharp object into a light source, which is what a soft drawn version can borrow.

ex-ferrofluid-2015.text: A deep-cut variant that swaps the wax for ferrofluid, so the moving part is a magnetic liquid rather than a melted solid.
behaviors: Its motion is not described in any fetched source, so a drawn copy needs checking
ex-ferrofluid-2015.principle: Changing the moving material changes the rhythm, so it is a separate reference rather than a colour swap.

ex-drawn-versions.text: Drawn versions tend to keep a tapered vessel, a bulb glow from below and a few large blobs, and the common failures come from blobs that are all one size and move at one speed.
behaviors: Uniform blob sizes read as a screensaver rather than wax
A glow that only lights the base reads as a light object, while a glow on the room reads as a lamp
ex-drawn-versions.principle: Drawn copies fail where the physics is quiet: wax that varies in size and speed, and light that follows the vessel, carries the look.

moodboard._about: Images collected from the scraped pages and the five Wikimedia Commons picks, looked at, and described. Only eight are described; the rest are listed under skipped. Photo samples are measured from the images, not print values.

signals: tapered glass column with a narrow cap
brushed gold cylindrical base widening to a foot
teal wax blobs on teal liquid
mb-vessel-straight-gold.text: Tall tapered glass body on a brushed base that flares at the foot; the wax reads as rounded blobs of the same hue as the liquid.

one pale blue wax blob low in the frame
mb-vessel-blue-close.text: Close view of a tapered vessel with a dark base cone; the wax sits low and glows lighter than the liquid.

mb-red-at-rest.term: red wax at rest on a warm yellow-orange liquid

mb-red-at-rest.text: Lamp at rest with red wax settled near the base in amber liquid, lit from inside against a warm wall.

mb-blk-in-operation.term: lamp in operation, wax columns on dark ground

pink liquid with a glowing base
rounded blob split off the column

mb-blk-in-operation.text: Wax stretches into a stalk from a bright base, with a rounded head and a smaller split-off blob, against a pink liquid.

books and a plant beside it
mb-windowsill-room.text: Lamp sits small in the frame, part of a shelf with objects; the room's coloured wall light is the main glow around it.

mb-astro-silver-hourglass.term: silver hourglass base lamp, red wax in violet liquid
signals: red wax rising in a column
mb-astro-silver-hourglass.text: A waisted silver base under a violet vessel, with a red column of wax and a yellow glow from the foot.

mb-astro-cyan-glow.term: cyan lamp with a bright lower glow
signals: pale teal wax mass near the top
mb-astro-cyan-glow.text: Cyan liquid lit from below, with a large pale wax mass in the upper half and a glowing green base.

mb-mathmos-rocket.term: rocket-form silver lamp on an orange room
signals: silver capsule with fins at the base
mb-mathmos-rocket.text: A silver rocket-form lamp with a purple vessel and red wax, set in a saturated orange room as a product shot.

mb-palette-samples.term: measured palettes of the eight described images
mb-palette-samples.text: Top colours by pixel share. Samples include the backdrop and room, so read them as photo values.

mb-shared-form-and-glow.term: shared shape and light in the eight described images
mb-shared-form-and-glow.text: Across the described images the vessel, base and wax are similar, and the glow sits in one of several places: lower third, mid-vessel, or evenly through the vessel.
behaviors: Lower third: the brightest band sits near the heat, so the base reads as the source
Mid-vessel: the brightest band sits in the middle, so the wax reads as suspended
Evenly through the vessel: the whole body glows at one level, so the form reads as a lit object rather than a hot spot
mb-shared-form-and-glow.principle: Where the glow sits tells the eye where the heat is; each placement reads differently, and the source layout picks which one.

anatomy._about: The parts of a drawn lava lamp and how they sit together, with proportions and the form decision. Built on the researched parts and cycle facts in the draft; the form and cap options are choices, not requirements.

options._about: options, not requirements: builder choices the sources do not decide

opt-form-classic.text: A tall tapered bottle over a bulb base, the silhouette most people picture. Tradeoff: most familiar, least stylised.

opt-form-globe.text: A round vessel with a short neck and a smaller cap. Tradeoff: reads as a lamp in general, but loses the tapered cue of the 1960s product.

opt-form-flat.text: Flat shapes, no glass shading, blobs as simple ovals. Tradeoff: easy to draw and animate, reads less physical, so the glow carries more of the look.

opt-cap.text: The fetched pages do not describe the cap, so it is a builder choice: a flat disc closing the vessel, or a rounded top tapering into it. Tradeoff: flat reads as a product, rounded reads as a lamp.

anx-base.text: A base that carries the bulb and the wire coil under the vessel; the bulb is the heat source for the whole cycle.
behaviors: The coil breaks the surface tension of cooled blobs so they merge again
Switching the bulb off stops the rise, and the wax settles to the base
anx-base.principle: One heat source runs the whole cycle, and the coil resets the wax each pass.

anx-wax.text: The moving solid: a wax that is lighter than its liquid when warm and sinks back when it cools.
properties: lighter than the liquid when warm
settles at the base when cool
behaviors: The density shift has to be tuned against the liquid, so small heat changes flip the wax
A cloudy melt clears only after several heat cycles
anx-wax.principle: The wax sits a little lighter or heavier than its liquid; small heat changes flip it.
signals: blobs stretching before they break free

tokens.blob_count: 3 to 5 large blobs; 15 to 30 small blobs that merge and split

anx-size.text: The classic lamp is a desk or floor object; the frame decides whether it reads as a small object or fills the picture.
behaviors: A tall lamp fills the frame height and its blobs read at a distance
A desk-scale lamp in a wide frame reads small, so its blobs need more contrast
anx-size.principle: Frame scale changes how many blobs read at once.

tokens.frame_height_share: 0.6 to 0.9 when tall in frame; 0.25 to 0.4 in a wide scene

anx-stack.text: From bottom to top: base with bulb and coil, a liquid column in a tall glass vessel, wax at the floor of the vessel when cool, and a cap closing the top.
properties: wax pools on the floor when cool
behaviors: The bulb heats the wax at the bottom, so the first blobs leave from the base area
Blobs travel the full vessel height, so the vessel height sets how long a rise takes
anx-stack.principle: The order of the parts follows the heat path: source at the base, the vessel carrying the cycle, a cooler top.
signals: wax at the base when cool

anx-liquid.text: The clear or translucent fluid the wax moves through, water or mineral oil based, sometimes tinted.
behaviors: A clear liquid shows the blob edges sharply; a tinted one softens the outline
anx-liquid.principle: The liquid's clarity sets how much the blob shapes read.
signals: blob edges visible through the liquid

tokens.tint: clear; pale amber; deep red, each reading differently

anx-vessel.text: A glass body over the bulb. Three shapes are common, and each changes how the wax moves: classic taper, squat globe, cylinder.
properties: classic taper: narrows toward the top
cylinder: same width top to bottom
behaviors: Classic taper: a wider bottom holds more wax near the heat, and a narrower top slows blobs as they climb
Squat globe: short height, so a blob crosses the vessel in less time
Cylinder: even width, so blobs keep a steady size as they climb
anx-vessel.principle: The shape sets the silhouette and how far the blobs travel; each shape reads as a different lamp.

tokens.height_to_bottom_width: 2.5 to 4 for a tall slim vessel; 1.2 to 1.6 for a squat globe

anx-cap-shapes.text: The cap closes the top of the vessel. Its shape changes the top silhouette and how blobs leave the surface; the sources do not settle which shape is used.
behaviors: Flat disc: a hard top edge that reads as a product
Rounded dome: a soft top that reads as a lamp
Tapered neck: the vessel narrows into the cap, so blobs slow as they reach the top
anx-cap-shapes.principle: The cap sets the top edge of the frame, and each shape reads as a different object.

anx-base-shapes.text: The base holds the bulb and coil under the vessel. Its shape changes the silhouette and where the bulb sits.
behaviors: Cone base: the bulb sits at the narrow point, so the glow spreads up and out
Cylinder base: the bulb sits inside a straight column, so light leaves evenly around it
Disc base: the bulb sits on a low flat plate, so the glow reads as a pool on the surface
anx-base-shapes.principle: The base shape decides how the bulb's light reaches the vessel.

motion._about: How the wax moves over time (facets only). No fetched source gives a period, speed, heat-up time or blob timing: the Gizmodo and TAMU pages state none, and the Wikipedia and primer sources give the cycle without numbers. Durations here are illustrative spreads, labelled as such.

options._about: options, not requirements: builder choices where the prompt and evidence are silent

opt-few-large.text: Two to four large blobs that take a long time to rise: the classic read, calm and easy to follow.

opt-many-small.term: many small blobs that merge and split
opt-many-small.text: Eight or more blobs of mixed size that merge and pinch off: busier, closer to a fluid in motion, and more places for uniform timing to show.

opt-click-stir.text: A click that speeds the heat or stirs the blobs: an interactive reading, relevant only if the lamp is meant to respond.

mo-timing.text: No fetched source gives a timing. These are starting spreads: a brisk lift, a slow lift and a near-still drift, with the sink usually quicker than the rise. Tune by eye.
behaviors: A short rise reads as a jolt, a long one as wax
A slow rise paired with a quicker sink reads as a convecting fluid rather than a slideshow
mo-timing.principle: Pace sets the character: the lamp reads as wax at a slow tempo and as a timer or a sprite at a fast one.
signals: rise under 4 s reads as a jolt
rise over 20 s reads as near-still

warm_up_s: 30 to 90, the first rise waits on the heat

mo-stretch-merge-split.text: Wax stretches as it lifts and pinches off into blobs. Cooled blobs pool at the base and merge; the coil in the base is what lets them merge and separate again.
behaviors: A blob stretches before it breaks free from the mass
Cooled blobs pool and merge at the bottom
Blobs can merge at the top or bottom and then part again on the next pass
mo-stretch-merge-split.principle: Merging and splitting are surface-tension events set off by the coil and the cool base, so the motion keeps changing shape.
signals: blobs that stretch and pinch off
merge at the top or bottom

mo-rest-and-loop.term: starting at rest and the loop
mo-rest-and-loop.text: A cool lamp rests with its wax settled at the bottom. The bulb warms it, the first blobs rise once the wax is warm enough, and the cycle repeats. No source gives a fixed period.
behaviors: Wax settled at the bottom when cool is the rest state
Heating restarts the rise from the pooled wax
Blobs that start at different times keep the cycle from looking like a repeated loop
mo-rest-and-loop.principle: Rest is the cool, pooled state; a start from rest is a warm-up, not a jump to full motion.
signals: flat pool at the base at start
first blobs appear after a delay

mf-convection-label.text: The rise-cool-sink description matches a convection loop. The TAMU page does not use the word convection, so this label is the builder's reading of the stated cycle.
properties: closed cycle of rising and sinking wax
mf-convection-label.principle: Heat lowers density, buoyancy lifts the wax, and cooling at the top lets it sink: the stated cycle is convection.

mo-easing.text: Easing sets how each blob starts and stops. Varying the curve per blob keeps the lamp from reading as mechanical.
signals: every blob on the same curve

curves: ease-in-out (cubic): smooth start and stop, the usual wax feel
ease-out (quad) on the lift: quick start, long settle near the top
ease-in on the sink: gathers speed as the wax falls
linear: constant speed, reads as a sprite rather than wax
overshoot spring: a bounce at the top, reads as a rubber toy

mo-blob-size-and-pinch.text: Blob radius spreads from small beads to fat lobes, and a blob stretches into a neck before it pinches off the mass.
behaviors: A small blob rises quickly and reads as a bead
A stretch past two times its length thins the neck until the blob pinches off
A fat blob holds its shape and moves more slowly
mo-blob-size-and-pinch.principle: Size and stretch set how a blob breaks free: small beads separate easily, and fat lobes stretch first.
signals: a thin neck before a blob breaks free

stretch_ratio: 3 to 4, a long thread before pinch-off

mo-warm-up-and-drift.text: The lamp waits on heat before the first rise, then a blob may hold a beat at the top before it sinks.
behaviors: A warm-up of 30 seconds reads as a lamp coming on, and 90 seconds reads as a slow heat-up
A pause at the top reads as weight, not a glitch
A near-still drift over 25 to 40 seconds reads as wax floating rather than moving
mo-warm-up-and-drift.principle: The warm-up and the top hold set when motion starts and how long each blob lingers.
signals: first blobs appear after a delay
a blob hangs at the top before it sinks

warm_up_s: 30 to 90, the first rise waits on the heat
pause_top_s: 0.5 to 1, a brief beat that reads as weight
1.5 to 2, a longer hold that reads as a lazy drift

light_and_setting._about: How the lamp is lit, the glow on the room, wax and liquid colour, and room tone. Sourced facts are the bulb and the wax cycle; colours beyond the pale column pieces are proposed readings, not sampled values.

options._about: options, not requirements: colour and glow readings with no sampled values; each names what it does to the lamp and the room

opt-light-warm-amber.text: Warm amber from the bulb: the wax reads gold to orange and the room stays warm and dim.
behaviors: Amber core fading to a deeper orange at the edge of the glow

opt-light-cool-violet.text: Cool blue-violet light: the wax reads lilac against a near-black room, and the lamp looks like a light source in its own right.
behaviors: Violet core cooling to blue at the edge

opt-light-multi-set.text: A set of hues (for example amber, rose and teal), each a separate colourway of the same lamp.
behaviors: Each hue runs its own cycle of rise and sink
A colour change reads as a new lamp, not a shift in the same one

opt-room-warm-wall.term: warm wall with a soft halo
opt-room-warm-wall.text: A dark warm wall behind the lamp, with the glow spilling onto it in a soft halo.
behaviors: The halo ties the lamp to the room
signals: soft halo on the wall behind

opt-room-near-black.text: A near-black or deep navy background so the glow carries the frame.
behaviors: The lit vessel is the brightest shape in the frame

lt-from-below.term: lit from below through the bottle
lt-from-below.text: A bulb in the base heats the tall glass bottle from below, and the wax warms and rises through the liquid.
properties: incandescent or halogen bulb in base
heat reaches the wax through the bottle
behaviors: The wax nearest the bulb is the first to lift off
The lower part of the vessel glows brightest
Glow fades toward the cap, so the top reads darker
lt-from-below.principle: The light and the motion share one source, so the glow is the heat that moves the wax.

lt-glow-falloff.term: glow and falloff on the room
lt-glow-falloff.text: How the light falls on the room depends on how many sources there are and where they sit. One low source gives the classic pool of light; two or more sources each give a different read.
properties: one low source: pool of light
two or more sources: overlapping glows
behaviors: One low source: a steep falloff keeps the room dim and the lamp as the focus
Two or more sources placed apart: each adds its own hotspot, and the room reads lit
Two equal sources on the lamp: a flatter, catalogue-style glow; a dimmer second source adds depth
lt-glow-falloff.principle: Light that shows where its source sits makes the lamp read as lit; the layout of sources sets which read the viewer gets.

lt-colour-readings.text: Three colour readings for the light: warm incandescent amber, cool tinted violet, and multi-colour. The sources give the warm bulb only; a cool colour needs a tinted bulb or filter, which the sources do not describe.
behaviors: Warm amber: gold to orange wax in a warm, dim room; matches the sourced bulb
Cool violet: lilac wax against a dark room; needs a tinted bulb or filter, which the sources do not describe
Multi-colour: each hue is a separate colourway with its own rise and sink
lt-colour-readings.principle: Colour sets the mood of the lamp. The sourced bulb is warm, so the violet and multi-colour readings are builder choices.

lexicon._about: Vocabulary and associations around the lava lamp: seed material that widens the search. Tier 3 and 4, inferred. None of it defines the object; the request does. Items marked deep cut are the ones a model would not say first.

lx-descriptors.text: People say lava lamp, wax lamp or blob lamp, and call the look groovy, retro or mod.

lx-sensory-mood.text: The lamp is slow and quiet: it looks viscous, warm and gently lit, and it calms the room.
